items.question: What should the yogic radiance be recognized as and what effect does it have?
premises: A specific radiance has been described previously
That radiance is to be known as nectar
This nectar destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: The yogic radiance is to be recognized as nectar that removes wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: One should know that to be nectar, which destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What bodily conditions are removed by attaining this nectar?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair
The practitioner becomes devoid of all diseases
items.inference: Attaining this nectar results in freedom from aging signs and all diseases.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and devoid of all diseases.

items.question: Where should the tongue be applied to bring about the destruction of disease?
premises: The tongue is the instrument of practice
The root of the palate is the prescribed location
The purpose is the destruction of disease
items.inference: Applying the tongue at the root of the palate serves to destroy disease.
items.plain_english: One should apply the tongue at the root of the palate for the destruction of disease.

items.question: How should the tongue be positioned continually within one's own mouth?
premises: The tongue should be contracted
The practice should be done always
The tongue should be united with one's own mouth
items.inference: The tongue should always be contracted and kept united within one's own mouth.
items.plain_english: One should always contract the tongue, keeping it united within one's own mouth.

items.question: What mental placement leads the practitioner to the state beyond mind?
premises: The mind is to be placed in the heart
This placement is maintained until a higher state is reached
The goal is the state of unmanatā
items.inference: Placing the mind in the heart leads the practitioner to the transcendent state beyond mind.
items.plain_english: Having placed the mind in the heart, one continues until the state beyond mind is attained.

items.question: What closely guarded secret regarding time is now being revealed to the goddess?
premises: The deception of time is a secret teaching
This teaching was well guarded
It is now made manifest
items.inference: The well-guarded secret of deceiving time has now been revealed.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the well-guarded secret of deceiving time has now been made manifest.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section concerning the emergence from the moon island?
premises: The context is the emergence from the moon island
A chapter is being marked as complete
It is identified as the sixth
items.inference: The sixth chapter concludes in the context of emergence from the moon island.
uncertainties: candra-dvīpa-vinirgate may refer to a specific textual section or yogic event
items.plain_english: Thus ends the sixth chapter in the section on the emergence from the moon island.

items.question: What teaching does the goddess request after declaring the lord as her sole refuge?
premises: The goddess has taken the lord as her sole refuge
She addresses the lord directly
She requests instruction on the three principles
items.inference: Having taken the lord as her sole refuge, the goddess asks to be taught the three principles.
items.plain_english: O Lord, tell me of the three principles; I have come to you alone as my refuge.

items.question: How should the object within the goddess's wheel be contemplated in its initial phase?
premises: Something within the goddess's wheel is to be contemplated
An analogy is drawn to the moon
The analogy specifies the first lunar day
items.inference: What is in the goddess's wheel should be contemplated like the moon on the first lunar day.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel, just as the moon appears on the first day of the lunar fortnight.

items.question: Where is the subtle flame said to be absorbed within the yogic body?
premises: A flame is present in that location
The flame is absorbed
The location is the bone wheel
items.inference: The flame is absorbed there in the bone wheel.
uncertainties: asthi-cakre may refer to a specific subtle center
items.plain_english: O beautiful-faced one, there indeed the flame is absorbed in the wheel of bone.

items.question: What qualities and effects characterize the form contemplated in this practice?
premises: The form is fluid and black
This form has a specific effect
The effect is the destruction of wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: The contemplated form is fluid and black, and it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: It is a fluid, black form, and it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What kind of yogic practice should be applied at the region of the support base?
premises: The location is the region of the support base
Yogic union is to be applied there
The practice is characterized as cool
items.inference: A cooling yogic practice should be applied at the region of the support base.
uncertainties: ādhāra-skandha-saṃsthāne may refer to a specific anatomical or subtle location
items.plain_english: One should apply a cooling yogic practice at the location of the support base.

items.question: How should the sun and moon be regarded in this yogic visualization?
premises: The sun is to be seen as an enemy
The moon is to be seen as a friend
Both are objects of deliberate visualization
items.inference: In this practice, the sun should be regarded as an enemy and the moon as a friend.
items.plain_english: One should see the sun as an enemy and the moon indeed as a friend.

items.question: What kind of physical location is suitable for undertaking this practice?
premises: The place may be an earthen house or solitary spot
The place must be free from disturbances
It should be devoid of gnats and mosquitoes
items.inference: The practice should be undertaken in a solitary place, such as an earthen house, free from gnats and mosquitoes.
items.plain_english: In an earthen house or a solitary place, free from gnats and mosquitoes.

items.question: What further qualities define the ideal environment for this yogic practice?
premises: The place should be secluded and deserted
The place should have a divine quality
The place should be adorned with many flowers
items.inference: The ideal environment is secluded, deserted, divine, and adorned with many flowers.
items.plain_english: In a secluded, deserted, divine place adorned with an abundance of flowers.

items.question: What level of attainment is realized after six months of this practice?
premises: The practice is performed over six months
Perfection becomes known after this period
The attainment is equal to the state of a yogini
items.inference: After six months, perfection is attained equal to the state of a yogini.
items.plain_english: After six months, perfection is known, equal to the state of a yogini.

items.question: From which knot onward are the three elements said to be situated?
premises: Three elements are being identified
Their location is specified relative to a knot
The starting point is the brahma knot
items.inference: The three are situated beginning from the brahma knot.
uncertainties: The referent of trīṇi and etāṃ depends on context
items.plain_english: O beautiful-faced one, these three are indeed situated beginning from the brahma knot.

items.question: What substance should be used to permeate the body beginning with the pores?
premises: A fluid is the instrument of the practice
The entire body is to be colored or permeated
The process begins with the pores of the skin
items.inference: One should permeate the entire body, beginning with the pores, with the fluid.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should color the entire body, beginning with the pores, with the fluid.

items.question: Within what timeframe is the promised result said to occur without doubt?
premises: The result is asserted to occur
There is no doubt about the result
The timeframe is within six months
items.inference: The result occurs without doubt within six months.
items.plain_english: It indeed happens without doubt within six months.

items.question: What visual and sonic qualities adorn the contemplated fluid form?
premises: The form is fluid and black in color
The form is adorned with additional elements
It is adorned with the sixteen vowels
items.inference: The contemplated form is fluid, black, and adorned with the sixteen vowels.
items.plain_english: It is fluid, black in color, and adorned with the sixteen vowels.

items.question: What rejuvenating transformation occurs through six months of dedicated practice?
premises: The practice is performed for six months
The practice is repeated and dedicated
Even an old person undergoes transformation
items.inference: Through six months of dedicated practice, even an old person becomes youthful.
items.plain_english: Through six months of dedicated practice, even an old person becomes youthful.

items.question: What dark-colored form is accessed by resorting to the place of the yogini?
premises: The practitioner resorts to the place of the yogini
A specific form is encountered there
The form is dark and black-colored
items.inference: By resorting to the place of the yogini, one accesses a dark, black-colored form.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to the place of the yogini, one encounters a dark, black-colored form.

items.question: Which bodily regions are to be colored by the splendor of that form?
premises: The splendor of the form is the instrument
Specific bodily regions are targeted
The regions include the hair, shoulder area, and skull
items.inference: One should color the regions of the hair, shoulders, and skull with its splendor.
uncertainties: keśa-skandha-kapāla-sthaṃ may refer to specific subtle or physical locations
items.plain_english: One should color the areas of the hair, shoulders, and skull with its splendor.

items.question: What ultimate freedoms from aging and affliction result from this practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from old age and death
The practitioner becomes devoid of disease and illness
items.inference: This practice results in freedom from old age, death, disease, and illness.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and illness.
